rule: A value change reads as a form change.
A strong 1-2-3 read: top lightest, light-facing side mid value, shadow side darkest, with the light placed high and to one side.
The core shadow is a dark band starting at the terminator and lightening onto the shadow side as reflected light increases.
Occlusion shadows are darkest where surfaces meet and in cavities and crevices, where less reflected light reaches.
The upper lip is one long, thin wrapping cylinder (with its own core shadow and cast shadow).
A cast shadow edge is sharper the closer the casting edge is to the surface receiving the shadow.
An eye reads as a reflective sphere: map the environment as a reflection on it, or use a single reflective highlight.
